notes: needs-triage vs ready-for-agent
Whether an empty note is allowed
Open questions on correcting a non-current action and correcting a correction, given as A/B/C with recommendations
Added Requirement and Acceptance criteria sections not named in the skill
Per case (new / old / no_subskills): grill 7/7, 5/7, 7/7; spec 8/8, 8/8, 5/8; implementer 6/7, 6/7, 7/7; code review 8/8, 7/8, 8/8; business review 8/8, 5/8, 8/8; finish 6/8, 0/8, 4/8.

Sub-skills with a measured effect: to-spec (without it the spec lost user stories, seams and out-of-scope: 8/8 -> 5/8) and retro (without it no deterministic check and the late-ADR gap was missed: 6/8 -> 4/8).

Sub-skills with no measured effect in these cases: grilling + domain-modeling (no_subskills also wrote ADR 0005 and GLOSSARY.md, because the deliver step and CLAUDE.md already ask for them), tdd (all three ran red then green), ponytail-review and code-review (planted defects were caught equally without them). The assertions were not built to isolate these skills, so this is 'not shown', not 'shown useless'.

What separated new from old was the text of /deliver and the repo rules, not the sub-skills: ADR instead of editing the frozen doc (grill), the dependency check (code review), the superseding-ADR and Doc impact checks (business review), and the AI log + retro (finish).

Eval defects: finish fixture already held the #17 row and cases C3-C5, so two 'adds' assertions were impossible for new and no_subskills (both correctly corrected the entries instead); the implementer scope assertion ('at most a doc line') penalises the Doc impact behaviour the new skill asks for; grill assertions 2 and 6 and most code-review assertions pass in every configuration; business-review old_skill findings were condensed by the orchestrator after a hook blocked the subagent's file write. One run per configuration, so no variance estimate.
Cost: the new version takes about 50 s and 14k tokens more per step than the old one (+28% time, +18% tokens); no_subskills sits in between.
